_comment: First-load JS per route, gzipped, in kilobytes — what a modern browser actually downloads. Legacy noModule polyfills are excluded. Raising a number here is a deliberate, reviewable act; see docs/REBUILD-PLAN.md M0.
_baselineNote: Measured shared floor: every asset `/_not-found` loads, which is every asset every route loads. Re-measured from 134 on 4 Sep 2026, and the correction matters more than the number. 134 was the *framework* alone — React 19 + Next 16's shared runtime — and the note here used to claim the default below therefore left '~24 kB for route-specific code'. It did not. The app shell is on every route too, and it is not free: react-dom 71.3 + the app-router runtime 42.9 + Next internals ~20 = ~134 kB of framework, then ~23.5 kB of shell (the session provider and its fetch, the top bar, the bottom nav, the drawer with its focus trap, the theme store, the share sheet, and the six icons that survive tree-shaking). 134 + 27 = 161 was therefore a ceiling that left 3.5 kB for a route's own code, not 24 — which is why seven routes sat marginally over it while every one of them was well inside what the budget intended to allow. 157.5 → 158.9 on 5 Sep 2026, and this one IS growth rather than a correction: the session cache (`src/lib/session/*`) is shell code, so every route pays it. Measured on the same tree, `/_not-found` 157.5 → 158.9, measured against HEAD with every other pending change reverted, so the 1.4 kB is this and nothing else. What it buys is in `_sessionCacheNote` below.
_raisedNote: 155 → 158 (production hygiene batch) → 161 (app menu, M20/M21) → 168 (re-baseline, 4 Sep 2026). The first two raises were the shell growing and were measured as such. The third is a different kind of change and should not be read as a fourth raise: nothing got bigger. The baseline was corrected from framework-only to the actual shared floor, and the default was re-derived from it as floor + 10.5 kB of route allowance. Measured route-specific cost on the day of the change — total minus the 157.5 kB floor — was /my-details 1.2, /for-you 3.4, /saved 3.7, /profile 4.9, /quiz 5.1, / 6.5, /updates 7.4, /jobs 8.0, /tracker 15.7 kB. The 10.5 kB allowance clears all but /tracker, which keeps an override below, and leaves roughly 2 kB of headroom on /jobs, the heaviest route that fits. That is deliberately tight: the point of this file is to make the next unreviewed import fail, and a default of 181 — the ~24 kB the original note intended — would have been loose enough to hide a real regression on a light route. To re-derive after a framework upgrade: build, then read the `/_not-found` row from `pnpm budget`; that figure is the floor. 168 → 169.4 (5 Sep 2026): the floor moved 1.4 kB and the default moved with it, by the same formula — floor + 10.5 kB of route allowance. The allowance is deliberately unchanged, so this grants no route any new room for its own code; it keeps the check measuring what it was measuring before the shell grew. Left at 168, /jobs would have sat 0.5 kB under its ceiling, and the next edit to /jobs would have failed for something that happened in the shell instead.
_sessionCacheNote: The 1.4 kB the shell grew by on 5 Sep 2026, named so a later reader can judge whether it still earns its place. `SessionProvider` starts `ready: false` and every save button, track button and avatar renders inert until `/api/session` answers — a round trip of a page that looks signed out to someone who is not, and on a dead network the full 8s `guardedFetch` deadline. The cache seeds all of it from the previous answer in one frame, then verifies against the server exactly as before. What the kilobytes are: `cache.ts` — the localStorage entry and the structural check that refuses a malformed one; `auth-cookie.ts` — reassembling the chunked Supabase session cookie and reading the user id out of it, which is what keys the entry so one account's shortlist can never be painted for the next person on the same browser; and ~0.1 kB in the provider for the seed and for telling 'the server said you are signed out' apart from 'the server did not answer'. What it deliberately does NOT ship: any dependency (`atob` and `TextDecoder` are platform), any change to what is fetched, and any caching of public data — jobs and updates are static and CDN-served already, so a client copy of them would save no read and risk showing a closed vacancy as open.
_routesNote: Per-route ceilings, for a route that carries something the others do not. Each entry names what the extra kilobytes buy, so a later reader can judge whether they still buy it. /calendar (161.3) and /syllabus (160.8) had overrides here and no longer need them: both sit under the re-baselined default, and their notes are kept below because what they record about those routes is still true.
_calendarNote: 159 → 161.2, ceiling set to 164. /calendar was a pure Server Component route: a month grid of links, no client JavaScript of its own. It now carries `CalendarView`, which is a Client Component by requirement — the month is local state so that paging between months costs no network at all, and selecting a day opens the day sheet in place. Measured on the same tree against the routes that ship no route-specific client code (/countdown 159.1, /my-details 158.7), so ~2.1 kB is the whole cost of the feature. What the 2.1 kB buys: the 42-cell grid with its dot stacking and today marker, the month cursor and its two buttons, the day sheet, the urgent/upcoming grouping, and the date chips. What it deliberately does NOT ship: the reads and the dedupe/precedence rules, which are server-side in `queries/calendar.ts`, and any new dependency — `Link`, the icon set, `useToday` and `format/deadline` were all already in the shared chunk, which is why a 600-line component costs two kilobytes. 164 rather than 161.5: the ~3 kB of headroom the earlier raises kept, and which `_trackerNote` records the loss of as a mistake. Override removed on 4 Sep 2026: at 161.3 kB the route is comfortably under the re-baselined 168 default, so a dedicated ceiling would only obscure it.
_syllabusNote: 159.2 → 160.7. The route carries the syllabus finder's typeahead, which is a Client Component by requirement: it filters as you type and opens on focus. Measured at each step on the same tree — 159.2 before the feature, 160.7 with it — so 1.5 kB is the whole cost, and it is worth naming what it is NOT. It is not the suggestion data (that is server-rendered into the document, which `pnpm budget` does not count and which measured 16.0 → 17.5 kB gzipped), it is not `syllabusKey` or the popular-exams table (both precomputed in `suggestions.ts`, which is what took the first build from 160.7 down to 160.2), and it is not the printable syllabus sheet (dynamic-imported on click, on the detail route). What the 1.5 kB buys: the combobox and its dropdown, the two suggestion groups with their headings, the exam/vacancy/cached row variants, and the substring filter that replaced two Supabase selects per keystroke. 161 → 163 rather than to 160.8: the default left 0.3 kB, which is the state `_trackerNote` below records as a mistake, and 2.3 kB restores the ~3 kB of room the earlier raises deliberately kept. Override removed on 4 Sep 2026, for the same reason as /calendar: 160.8 kB is under the re-baselined 168 default.
_trackerNote: 158 → 162 → 165. /tracker carries the exam status panel: the collapsed summary, the expanded stage/date/result detail, and the refresh button with its cooldown timer. Measured at 157.5 kB when the panel landed and 159.9 kB after the menu, which is the same 2.4 kB every other route paid — so 162 → 165 preserves the headroom the 162 was for, rather than granting new room. The panel is a Client Component by requirement: it owns a fetch, a countdown and a disclosure. What it deliberately does NOT ship is the parsing — `status-parse.ts` is server-only, and `report.ts` is imported here for pure accessors with no Zod behind them. 165 → 170: measured 169.0 kB at b49af12 — already over the 165 before this change, so the tracker redesign in that commit spent the headroom without moving the number — and 169.9 kB after `categorize.ts`, the 0.9 kB that groups a tracked exam into Action / Upcoming / Completed. It ships to the browser because the filter tabs regroup on click and the grouping re-derives at IST midnight; it adds no dependency, reusing `report.ts` accessors and `daysUntilFrom` that the route already carried. NOTE: this leaves 0.1 kB of headroom, not the ~3 kB the earlier raises kept. It is a ceiling raised to where the route already is, so the next import on /tracker fails the check — which is the intended behaviour, but means the next person here should expect to trim rather than to have room. 170 → 174 (re-baseline, 4 Sep 2026): not a raise. /tracker measures 173.2 kB, of which 157.5 is the shared floor every route pays and 15.7 kB is the route's own code — the status panel, the attempt list and form, the filter tabs and `categorize.ts`. It is the heaviest route in the app by a wide margin (the next is /jobs at 8.0 kB) and it is the one to look at first if the shell ever needs relief. 174 restores the ~1 kB of working room that the note above records losing, measured against the corrected floor. 174 → 175.5 (5 Sep 2026): not a raise either. /tracker measures 174.7, of which 158.9 is the new shared floor and 15.8 kB is the route's own code — unchanged, to a rounding error, from the 15.7 kB recorded above. The route grew by the 1.4 kB every route grew by, and 175.5 keeps the same ~0.7 kB of working room it had before. It is still the heaviest route in the app and still the first place to look for relief.
_unmeasuredNote: Routes that emit no prerendered scripts because they are blocking (`export const instant = false`). They are never CDN-served, so first-load JS is not the figure that matters for them. Listing one here is a deliberate act: an unlisted route with no scripts still fails the build, so a route cannot drift out of measurement by accident.
